metadata.title: SpaceX IPO: Last-minute strategies on how you can invest

content.text:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure.
This is it. The day SpaceX launches its IPO and Elon Musk quite possibly becomes the world's first trillionaire.
Meanwhile, Anthropic and OpenAI are busily preparing for their own public stock introductions.
Missed your shot at buying some of the 555 million shares being offered in the SpaceX IPO? Here's a backup plan.
Read more: SpaceX's IPO dream runs into Wall Street's oldest test.
The SpaceX IPO: 'Oversubscribed' and driven by institutional investors
You may have heard that the SpaceX IPO is "four times oversubscribed." That simply means there is much more demand for the IPO shares than there is supply — one reason: Institutional investors are grabbing mountains of SpaceX stock.
BlackRock placed an order for $5 billion worth of SpaceX shares, according to the Wall Street Journal. Small investors are being squeezed nearly out of the market, though Elon Musk has said that he wanted to allocate 30% of the shares to individual investors.
SpaceX shares were available through five brokerage firms, including Charles Schwab, E-Trade, Fidelity, Robinhood, and SoFi. Each firm allocated its shares according to its own investor criteria.
SpaceX 's initial public offering will begin trading under the ticker symbol SPCX on Nasdaq.
Elon Musk has once again chosen an unconventional path by rejecting the usual IPO price range. Instead, the rocket and satellite company will open at a $135 share price, as confirmed by a statement issued by the company Thursday afternoon. Musk looks to raise $75 billion at a $1.75 trillion valuation.
Dive deeper into the SpaceX IPO
The public debut of Elon Musk's rocket and AI company is expected to make history.
Didn't get IPO shares from your broker? Place a limit order.
Buying SpaceX after today's open will be like walking a tightrope. First of all, there will be a very thin supply, perhaps just 3% to 4% of total shares, available for trade. That means there will likely be significant volatility, so consider placing a limit order to avoid a market-order shock.
Remember, your order might not clear today, as public trading will occur hours after the opening bell. You might want to make that limit order "good 'til canceled."
"We believe that SpaceX will use its expertise in engineering, manufacturing and space technologies to grow to the largest communications, cloud/AI company in the world, in our scenario," Oppenheimer said.
It's likely that SPCX will pop well above $135, and maybe even drop below the opening price — and that's why we recommend a limit order.
Just remember the age-old investing adage: "A good idea today is a good idea tomorrow." Don't let IPO fever keep you from making rational, prudent investment decisions that best suit your risk appetite and long-term investing goals.
Don't qualify for IPO shares? You may still get exposure.
For those of us who don't qualify for IPO shares, we may very well gain exposure to SpaceX in our 401(k) s or other index-based investments at some point. Recent rule changes allow IPO shares to have a shorter shelf life before being added to index funds.
However, S&P Dow Jones Indices announced that it's keeping the entry rules for major indexes intact, denying rapid entry to SpaceX and other mega IPOs. That means SpaceX will not be eligible for inclusion in the S&P 500 for at least a year following its public debut.
The Nasdaq will likely be your best option. It can allow a company to be added to its index after only 15 trading days. That means mutual funds and exchange-traded funds that mirror the Nasdaq may have some minor exposure to SpaceX.
Vanguard says that the weight in any index will initially be tiny — about 5% of the shares made available to the public.
"The resulting Vanguard portfolio changes for SpaceX are expected to be limited, as portfolio weights are anticipated at first to be 1% or less," the company said in a statement. "That should help keep turnover and tax impact low with little change to portfolio tracking."
Read more: SpaceX IPO is coming for your 401(k). Should you be concerned?
